title: Yes or no: the answer comes from your side

sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: A yes/no question uses the same words as a statement, and the answer changes the person to fit who answers: a question to *te* is answered with *én*, a question to *ti* with *mi*. A question about other people, *Anna és Károly olvasnak?*, is answered with the plural *Igen, olvasnak.*

sections.title: Saying no
sections.content: To say no, put *nem* before the verb, as before: *Nem, nem pihenünk.* The first *nem* is “no” and the second negates the verb.

items.english: Do you rest today? – Yes, I rest today.
Do you all rest today? – Yes, we rest today.

items.spanish: Anna és Károly ebédelnek? – Igen, ebédelnek.
items.english: Do Anna and Károly have lunch? – Yes, they have lunch.
Do you all rest? – No, we do not rest.

sections.content: Do not repeat the question's form. *Pihentek?* is answered *Pihenünk*, not *Pihentek*. Only a question about other people (*ők* or one person) is answered with the same form.
